body:
OWNER DISPOSITION on the two requested capabilities and the ZOOM/MAP questions.

ACCEPTED AS PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS.

ZOOM-1: durable. The primary gesture is focus-and-context navigation that crosses typed semantic representations while conserving Address and reading focus. Camera magnification may exist as a local convenience, but it is not semantic zoom. The Story/Episode/Scene buttons remain tracer controls until the interaction changes the compiled representation and proves V-L2 through OnMark, ViaAncestor with descent, or OffProjection.

ZOOM-2: yes, narrative grain and surface detail remain independently addressable. A linked gesture may move both by policy, but CommonViewState / AtlasSpec must not collapse NarrativeLevel and SurfaceDetail. FeatureScale remains the independent measurement basis; screen density is policy, not another scientific scale.

ZOOM-3: the Codex never substitutes a summary for exact words. Atlas focus should scroll or navigate the docked Codex to supporting text while preserving its exact-text tiling. Novel-scale DOM virtualization is an implementation detail only if the full compiled flow, stable offsets, selection, search, and deterministic remount are preserved.

MAP-1: when no recall is loaded, first sight is Codex plus Discourse Atlas. When a recall is loaded or selected, the default workspace becomes the story/recall split with the alignment matrix in the projection pane. The researcher may switch that pane back to Atlas or Loom without losing joined focus.

MAP-2: all three are replaceable faces of one mapping workspace: matrix first for posterior truth, dual rails for textual adjudication once the privacy-gated trace exists, voyage over Atlas or Loom for orientation. They are not separate applications.

MAP-3: focus is coupled; scale is not. Selecting a cell establishes the recall unit, story Address set, and full AlignState. Story and recall grains may then move independently, so an episode-level gist placement can still be inspected at token detail without rewriting the alignment state.

MAP-4: confirmed. External states, Unranked, Distorted facets, abstention, and unresolved mass are part of the mapping even when no source tether exists. A ribbon-only view is incomplete. Identity proof is not privacy authorization, and the recall text remains separately compiled under its own policy.

Instrument-map acceptance scenario: select a situation at Event/Tokens, zoom to Story/Hidden and observe ViaAncestor while the exact Codex focus remains, return to Event/Tokens and recover OnMark; then load a recall and see the matrix by default with Distorted and External cells still selectable. If either selection disappears, or if the only motion is optical scaling, the artifact fails.
